lines.text: Ten thousand requests waiting on I/O in Java: where does the bottleneck end up?
A thread runs one request, and in Java it holds an operating system thread, which is expensive, even when it's only waiting.
So the pool caps at two hundred, and the rest of the requests wait in line.
Switching the pool to virtual threads is a one-line change.
A virtual thread belongs to the JVM and doesn't hold an OS thread while it waits, so all ten thousand wait together.
But with only fifty connections at the database the line comes back there.
The pool of two hundred took five seconds, the virtual threads one hundred seventy-nine milliseconds, and with fifty connections it went back to twenty seconds.
The bottleneck went from the threads to the connections, and you, which limit would you size?
